open_obligations: Note that the product-of-wins model assumes step outcomes are independent, so it does not test error propagation directly.
Check that the equal-slope assumption (mG = mH = 1) used for the numerical results is realistic.
Check whether 'oversight success' in Engels et al. corresponds to bounded reward-model error in Leike et al.
out.other_title: Do errors accumulate across levels of recursive reward modeling?
out.rationale: Leike et al. ask whether mistakes compound across levels of recursive reward modeling. Engels et al. model nested oversight as a chain whose success is the product of stepwise Guard win probabilities and report that multiple steps can move Guard log odds from -3 to 3, with the optimal number of steps growing with the general capability gap; the model assumes independent steps on fitted Elo lines rather than measuring error propagation.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: how oversight success changes when weak-to-strong oversight is chained over several levels, in an Elo-based model of nested scalable oversight

open_obligations: Do not map Elo-model step counts onto finetuning bootstrapping chains.
Check whether Burns et al.'s tasks are Guard-favoured or Houdini-favoured in Engels et al.'s sense.
Note Engels et al.'s equal-slope assumption.
out.other_title: Bootstrapping through intermediate model sizes improves weak-to-strong PGR on chess
out.rationale: Burns et al. report bootstrapping through two intermediate sizes improves PGR on chess, especially for larger students, but helps little on NLP and not on reward modeling. Engels et al.'s numerical NSO model finds multiple oversight steps can raise Guard log odds from -3 to 3, with more steps optimal as the general capability gap grows, but one step optimal in Houdini-favoured games; one is a training experiment, the other an Elo model of adversarial oversight games.
out.scope: proposed SAME_QUESTION_DIFFERENT_SETTING: whether supervising a strong model through intermediate steps beats a single large weak-to-strong jump

text: From numerical evaluation of their NSO model with equal slopes (mG = mH = 1), the authors report that multiple oversight steps let Guards oversee much smarter Houdinis, sometimes moving Guard log odds from -3 to 3; that the optimal number of steps grows with Delta_general at fixed Delta_domain; that larger Delta_general at fixed Delta_domain makes oversight easier; and that in Houdini-favoured games (Delta_general < Delta_domain) one step appears optimal.
title: Numerical NSO findings: multi-step oversight beats one step as the capability gap grows
